name: Montenegrin First League
content:
The Montenegrin First League is the highest professional football division in Montenegro and was established in 2006 following the country’s independence. It is organized by the Football Association of Montenegro and represents the top tier of the national football league system. The competition replaced the previous joint league system that included Serbian clubs, marking a new era for domestic football in Montenegro.

The league typically consists of 10 teams that compete in a multi-round format, where each club plays against every other team several times throughout the season. Over the years, the structure has been adjusted, but the modern format generally involves a quadruple round-robin system, resulting in a long and competitive campaign. Teams aim not only for the national title but also for qualification spots in UEFA competitions.

Historically, the most successful clubs in the competition are Budućnost Podgorica and Sutjeska Nikšić, which have dominated most of the league titles since its formation. Other clubs such as Rudar Pljevlja, Zeta, and Mogren have also won championships in different seasons, but the title race is often primarily contested between the traditional powerhouses. The league also features promotion and relegation with the Montenegrin Second League, ensuring movement between divisions based on performance.

The Montenegrin First League is the top professional football division in Montenegro and was established in 2006 after the country became independent. It is organized by the Football Association of Montenegro and represents the highest level of domestic football competition. The league replaced the previous joint system that included clubs from Serbia and Montenegro, marking the beginning of a separate national football structure for Montenegro.

The competition generally features 10 teams, although the number has varied in earlier seasons. Clubs compete in a multi-round format where each team plays the others several times during the season, creating a long and competitive schedule. The league also serves as a qualification route for European tournaments, with top teams earning spots in UEFA competitions, which adds significant importance to final standings.

Since its formation, the league has been dominated mainly by FK Budućnost Podgorica and FK Sutjeska Nikšić, which have won most of the championships. Other clubs such as Rudar, Mogren, Zeta, and Dečić have also achieved title success, but less frequently. Promotion and relegation with the Montenegrin Second League ensure movement between divisions, maintaining competitiveness across seasons.
